audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart reads Galio/Galio/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill; content and packet read Skill/Skill/Galio/Skill/Ekko/Ekko/Ekko.
audit.why: Levels 1-2 are even — Ekko Q is 1075 against an 825 Winds of War, and the taunt needs 275 range Galio cannot reach. Level 3 is his because Shield of Durand into Justice Punch is a real kill pattern. From 6 on, Chronobreak (110s) duels and Hero's Entrance (180s) does not.
audit.corrected: Full rows aligned to content, whys rewritten to argue each row's verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never named the cooldowns that define the spikes: Justice Punch 11s, Shield of Durand 18s, Hero's Entrance 180s against Chronobreak's 110s.
audit.why: The 180s-versus-110s gap is the actual reason level 6 belongs to Ekko, and the page asserted the verdict without it.
audit.corrected: phases[4], phases[5], cooldowns and the content 'mid' paragraph now carry the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The taunt is attributed to the wrong ability across the content layer. Shield of Durand (W, 275 range, 18s) is the taunt; Justice Punch (E, 650 range, 11s) is a dash knockup. whys[2], wants.foe[0], wants.you[0] and spikes[0].text all call Justice Punch the taunt.
audit.why: Riot's text: Shield of Durand 'will taunt and damage nearby enemies'; Justice Punch 'knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters'. A reader spacing against the wrong ability at the wrong range gets caught.
audit.corrected: Both abilities named correctly with their own ranges and cooldowns throughout; Justice Punch also stated as the thing that stops Ekko's E mid-dash, and Colossal Smash flagged as the auto-reset wind-up tell.

audit.why: It is the field that must hold real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Now carries Justice Punch 11s, Shield of Durand 18s at 275 range, Hero's Entrance 180s, Chronobreak 110s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string and dontsFull[2].d the tradeBad string under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2).
audit.why: Bodies did not match their own titles.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to the W-pre-placement bullet and the trading-in-his-wave bullet respectively, grounded in Justice Punch's 650 range and the Colossal Smash area proc.

edits.after: Skill

edits.before: Q the wave and his toes — the return pass chunks; learn the slow zone's drag on his dodge patterns.
edits.after: Q both passes at 1075 range — his Winds of War is 825 and the taunt needs 275 he cannot reach.

edits.before: Galio
edits.after: Skill

edits.before: E blink-strike window opens: Q-E-auto is your first real trade and the third passive hit stings already.
edits.after: E opens the blink-strike, but Colossal Smash is his wind-up tell — step back on the swing, not the cast.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Galio

edits.before: W zone games begin: drop it on his retreat line BEFORE trading and the stun finds him mid-regret.
edits.after: Justice Punch knocks you up at 650 range and sets the taunt behind it — level 3 is his cleanest kill.

edits.before: Three-hit trades on cooldown — Q in, E the gap, passive proc, walk. Bank the tempo for 6.
edits.after: Q in, E the gap, passive proc, walk — stay outside 650 and Justice Punch has nothing to hit.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ekko

edits.before: Chronobreak online — your aggression gets a save file. Trade like the rewind exists, because it does.
edits.after: Chronobreak at 110s wins duels; Hero's Entrance is 180s and built for other lanes, not for this one.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ekko

edits.before: First item spike: the full string deletes half bars and the rewind erases the counter-argument.
edits.after: First item: his base damage cannot answer the full string, and the taunt is 18s between attempts.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ekko

edits.before: Late Ekko picks and survives: dive the carry, W the peel, and Chronobreak out of whatever they answered with.
edits.after: Late he is peel, not a duelist — take the pick behind him and Chronobreak out of the collapse that follows.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - R Chronobreak spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Justice Punch is 11s at rank 1 — the knockup, not the taunt, is what catches your E mid-dash. - Shield of Durand is the 18s taunt and only reaches 275: fight him outside it. - Hero's Entrance is 180s; your Chronobreak is 110s.

edits.before: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, walk out through the slow — the full string chunks and the return pass pays the exit.
edits.after: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, then leave — all three land before an 18s taunt can be charged at 275 range.

edits.before: Blinking in with R down against a loaded kit — Ekko without the rewind is a mid laner doing parkour at a funeral.
edits.after: Brawling inside 275 range — Shield of Durand taunts you into Justice Punch and the trade stops being yours.

edits.before: Good trade: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, walk out through the slow — the full string chunks and the return pass pays the exit. Bad trade: Blinking in with R down against a loaded kit — Ekko without the rewind is a mid laner doing parkour at a funeral.
edits.after: Good trade: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, then leave before he can charge a taunt you would have to stand inside. Bad trade: brawling within 275 range — Shield of Durand taunts, Justice Punch knocks you up, and the trade is his.

edits.before: Galio wins by landing Justice Punch, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Galio wins by charging Shield of Durand at 275 range, taunting your string away, and knocking you up on the way out.

edits.before: Carry through insured dives — one carry per rewind cycle; your job is spending R as a weapon, not an apology.
edits.after: Carry by fighting outside 275 range — no taunt reaches you there, and his base damage cannot close a string.

edits.before: His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Justice Punch is 11s — with it down he cannot reach you. Bait it, count it, then go.

edits.before: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, walk out through the slow — the full string chunks and the return pass pays the exit.
edits.after: Drop the anomaly behind you before stepping up — his only follow-up is a 650-range Justice Punch, and the stun beats it.

edits.before: Blinking in with R down against a loaded kit — Ekko without the rewind is a mid laner doing parkour at a funeral.
edits.after: Colossal Smash cleaves an area every few seconds — inside his wave that proc hits you and the minions together.

edits.before: Galio's Justice Punch taunt into a full combo gives him a real edge if he lands it during this window.
edits.after: Shield of Durand's taunt into Justice Punch gives him a real edge whenever he lands it in this window.

edits.before: Land Justice Punch to taunt and disrupt your combo mid-fight
edits.after: Land Shield of Durand to taunt and disrupt your combo mid-fight

edits.before: Avoid overextending into his Justice Punch taunt range
edits.after: Avoid overextending into his Shield of Durand taunt range

edits.before: Galio's Winds of War and Shield of Durand punish extended trades — if you overstay in melee range he taunts your engage away with Justice Punch, giving him a strong short window.
edits.after: Galio's Winds of War and Shield of Durand punish extended trades — overstay inside 275 range and the taunt lands, with Justice Punch knocking you straight back in for the rest of it.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 briefly tilt toward Galio if he lands a taunt into a full combo, since Shield of Durand's damage reduction lets him win a prolonged trade you'd otherwise take, but by level 6 your Chronobreak gives you a far stronger duel tool than his roam-oriented ultimate, flipping momentum clearly back to you.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 briefly tilt toward Galio if he charges Shield of Durand into a full combo, since the taunt holds you inside Winds of War long enough to win a trade you would otherwise take, but by level 6 your 110s Chronobreak is a far stronger duel tool than his 180s roam ultimate, flipping momentum back to you.

notes: Main correction: the content layer repeatedly called Justice Punch the taunt. Shield of Durand (W) is the taunt at 275 range on 18s; Justice Punch (E) is the 650-range dash knockup on 11s. Fixed in whys[2], wants.foe[0], wants.you[0], spikes[0].text and the 'mid' paragraph. I also dropped the claim that Shield of Durand grants 'damage reduction' — Riot's text says only that he charges a defensive stance and taunts on release, and the kit carries a shield flag, not a stated DR value. packet.suspectNames flags 'Bait Shield of Durand', 'Use Winds of War', 'Save Hero's Entrance' and 'Shield of Durand's' — all correct Riot names, all FALSE POSITIVES. Content win[] already matched the packet chart, so the side edits touch the full layer only and no paired win[N] edit exists. No report[] rewrites: none lint-flagged, none naming a fabricated ability — though report[5].t still carries the vague 'His dash knockup' phrasing and would be worth a sweep.
